correctness.rationale: For every finite-dimensional model of dimension \(N\), the least defect satisfies \(d(M)\leq\dim M_0\leq\dim M\) and \(d(M)\leq N-\dim M\), so \(N\geq2d(M)\). For each integer \(r\geq1\), the symbol \(g(z)=\overline z^{\,2r+2}+z^{4r+1}\) on \(K_{z^{4r+2}}\) and exact rank-\(r\) perturbation \(\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}e_{2j+1}\otimes e_{2j+2}\) yield an explicit kernel of dimension \(2r+1\). Under the perturbed operator, its shifted basis maps onto \(2r+1\) distinct signed coordinate vectors; hence its least defect is exactly \(2r+1\), attaining the minimal model dimension \(4r+2\). Equality forces every minimizing kernel to vanish at the origin and be complementary to its backward-shift image. The finite checks for ranks one through thirteen passed, but the all-ranks proof is symbolic.

value.rationale: This resolves the exact smallest scalar Hardy model dimension required to exhibit the known maximal near-invariance defect \(2r+1\) for rank-\(r\) truncated Toeplitz perturbations. The cutoff \(4r+2\) is intrinsic model complexity, attained within a constrained operator class rather than merely among arbitrary subspaces. Earlier all-rank witnesses used larger models. At this cutoff the kernel necessarily occupies half the model and is transverse to its backward-shift image. The result supplies the smallest testing examples in every rank; no new general upper defect bound or downstream theorem is asserted.
